title: List a chat's messages with paging and a filter
problem: messages_api.py has an app and an in-memory MESSAGES list, but no routes. Add GET /chats/{chat_id}/messages that returns that chat's messages newest first, with a capped limit, cursor-style paging via `before`, and an unread filter. Let FastAPI do the parsing and validation: no manual int() or bool parsing.
requirements: GET /chats/{chat_id}/messages returns {"chat_id": <int>, "messages": [...]} with each message dict unchanged
Messages are that chat's only, sorted by id descending (newest first)
Query `limit`: optional, default 20, must be between 1 and 100 inclusive; otherwise 422
Query `before`: optional int; when given, only messages with id < before
Query `unread_only`: optional bool, default false; when true, only messages with read == False
Filters (chat, before, unread_only) apply first, then the limit
edgeCases: A chat with no messages: 200 and an empty list, not an error
limit=1 and limit=100 are valid; 0 and 101 are 422
chat_id or before that isn't an int, and unread_only=maybe: 422 from FastAPI
unread_only accepts true/yes/on/1 like any FastAPI bool
Sorting MESSAGES in place would change the data for every later request
hints: Conceptual: one path parameter and three query parameters. Their types and defaults are the whole validation; your function body only filters, sorts and slices.
Specific: `limit` needs Annotated[int, Query(ge=..., le=...)] with a default of 20; `before` is optional with no value, so its default is None. Filter first, sort second, slice last.

Implementation: build a new list with a comprehension that keeps m when m["chat_id"] matches, before is None or m["id"] < before, and not (unread_only and m["read"]). Then sorted(..., key=lambda m: m["id"], reverse=True)[:limit].
evaluation: No manual parsing: types, defaults and Query constraints do the validation
sorted() on a new list, not MESSAGES.sort()
The limit is applied after filtering and sorting
